Beyond them, a row of dark holes in the far masonry promises a volley of something worse than arrows should the wires be pulled. I try to talk my way past the guard..narration:
You lean in and speak low, offering the guard a fiction woven from dungeon rumor and half-heard names—just enough shape to let his caution unravel into apathy. His grip on the spear slackens; he spits, turns the key in the rusted lock, and hauls the gate open with a shriek of iron that seems to offend the dark itself. He does not meet your eyes again. Beyond the threshold, the passage exhales cold, damp air from somewhere far below.
